groups.evidence: The machine-validated migration target contract fixes native dependency order, dry-run non-mutation, row/result states, duplicate identity, idempotency, exact reconciliation, cutover, rollback, privacy and evidence requirements. A bilingual submittable Bunood Migration Run freezes a mapped candidate packet with source hashes/row counts, source site and one-way database identity, mapping/evidence references, named owners, distinct material-opening review, cutover/backup/rollback controls and immutable scope/receipt digests. A guarded isolated-rehearsal path requires a different site/database plus explicit site opt-in, rechecks native permissions, verifies the exact attached file hash, runs Frappe's native Data Import, and captures an immutable privacy-minimised result receipt. Each Data Import dataset requires stable-identity evidence and an import-type-compatible duplicate disposition. Exact retry returns the existing rehearsal without enqueueing another job; exception correction creates a new draft bound to predecessor and receipt digest, and submission requires a material source/mapping/identity/duplicate/control-evidence change. A submitted exception receipt with failed rows can download Frappe's native errored-row template only after Bunood rechecks the isolated environment, receipt, packet, native import identity, current permissions and attached-file hash; Bunood does not proxy raw import logs. After every mapped Data Import dataset succeeds on the same clone, a submittable reconciliation record binds all successful receipt/result/file digests, preloads the eleven source-to-native control families, preserves exact decimal text and reproducible native report filters, derives exact/variance/exception state, requires owned recovery for every non-zero difference and enforces a different reviewer for material openings. It is immutable evidence, not a parallel ledger or accounting/cutover approval. No promoted migration run exists.
